requirements.summary: appworker user was created with adduser (uid 1001, shell /bin/ash, home /home/appworker), confirmed via id/getent both before and after a full node restart.

requirements.requirement: Login sessions for appworker limited to 8,192 open files
requirements.summary: Because Alpine's default su/login/sshd are not PAM-linked, the executor installed openssh-server-pam and shadow-login so /etc/security/limits.d is actually enforced, wrote appworker soft/hard nofile 8192, and directly verified nofile=8192/8192 on a real `su -l` session and a genuine network SSH login, both before and after a full node restart.

requirements.requirement: Login sessions for appworker limited to 256 processes
requirements.summary: Same limits.d config sets nproc soft/hard 256; verified nproc=256/256 on both su and real SSH login sessions before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all managed nodes (node1)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 0389d7d9... with healthy account/limits/sshd/su state (cmd-c643c825c739451b). Reboot acknowledgement returned immediately (cmd-473a20a11bfc4a56). Multiple connection-reset/timeout errors confirmed the node was down (cmd-126ff0a326d14e13, cmd-4f1c0e9cb103449d, cmd-10b9c233fb124388). Recovery showed a new boot_id c40cc5a3... (cmd-74392c8d7bbe4170), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot. Post-restart checks confirmed account, limits file, PAM-enabled sshd, su session, and live SSH session all recovered correctly (cmd-c594cf652c4d4453).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — creating the appworker account and enforcing an 8,192 open-file / 256-process limit on its login sessions — are satisfied with direct, repeated evidence via both `su -l` and genuine network SSH logins, both before and after a full node restart that confirmed persistence. The executor correctly diagnosed that Alpine's default non-PAM login stack would make limits.conf inert and fixed the root cause (PAM-enabled sshd/su via openssh-server-pam and shadow-login) rather than just dropping a config file. The independent restart-evidence protocol was also completed cleanly for node1, with boot-identity change, disruption, and full recovery all directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: A small residual file, /tmp/reboot.log, was left on node1 after the restart and not cleaned up, though it is low-risk and does not affect task functionality.
Verification relies on the executor's own captured command output rather than independent re-execution; no contradicting evidence was found.

operational_hygiene.summary: Overall hygiene is good. Package installs (openssh-server-pam, shadow-login) and sshd reconfiguration (SSHD_BINARY, UsePAM) were all necessary to make PAM limits enforcement actually work on Alpine's non-PAM-wired login stack, and are retained as required task state. Two earlier attempts to create the user/set the password failed midway (cmd-b7d3c9d5857b4aa2 due to missing openssl, cmd-b83978a765dc4201 due to a broken pipe in the password RNG chain) — these are corrective retries toward the same outcome, not unrelated experiments, and account creation was idempotent so no conflicting state resulted; the third attempt (cmd-974f30585d30466d) completed cleanly. Temporary SSH test keys (cmd-e387e7e648574d86, cmd-c594cf652c4d4453) were created and fully removed after use — bounded and reverted. The one residual item is /tmp/reboot.log, a small log file left behind by the backgrounded reboot command (cmd-473a20a11bfc4a56), visible as an added line in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; this is low-risk residue but was not cleaned up.
